analysis:
This batch is documentation only. It adds changelog.d/flint-serving-speedups.md (head lines 1-5) and inserts docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 2172-2184. Both describe Flint constrained-decode chaining and device mask caching keyed by constraint state (maskCacheKey). They also state that RecursiveSI/flint-int4 moves to the automatic paged list, serving at legacyMaximumConcurrency (8) on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. No source code is in this batch, so the documented behavior cannot be verified.

Security relevance:
(1) A mask cache keyed only on constraint state while output budget remains could be shared across concurrent requests. The mask encodes only the allowed token set for the protocol state, not prompt content, so no A-001 exposure is evident. Integration should confirm the cache is per-engine/per-model, holds no request-derived data, and that the budget-exhausted state is excluded from the key as documented.
(2) Chained decode redraws from retained logits, with penalty and RNG state restored. The claimed byte-identical output is a correctness claim (T-007/T-056 already cover correctness non-guarantees). The implementation must not leak retained logits across rows.
(3) Raising flint-int4 concurrency to 8 affects availability and memory admission (TB-007/T-029). Admission is said to remain per-request via existing CBv2 ledgers, but the SDK pin and ServingPerformanceProfiles source are not supplied.

The base text excerpt (Nemotron/GLM sections) is unchanged context. No threat-model assumption (T-041 cache scoping, TB-002 encryption) is altered by these doc changes. No regression was identified from the supplied evidence. The SDK pin and profile changes need source-level review elsewhere.
